COURT’S OR JUDGES’S ORDERS
C482 No.819 of 2023
Hon’ble Sharad Kumar Sharma, J.
Mr. Kanti Ram Sharma, Mr. Deepak 
Vaswani, Advocates, for the applicants.
Mr. Pratiroop Pandey, AGA, for the State 
of Uttarakhand.
The present C482 application arises out of 
a matrimonial dispute, wherein, the present 
applicants have been summoned to be tried for 
the offences under section 498A, 323 and 504 of 
IPC, and ¾ of the Dowry Prohibition Act. 
Though, it is stated at the bar, that there 
happens to be a corresponding proceedings for 
restitution of conjugal rights which is pending, in 
which the respondent/complainant has not put in 
appearance, despite of service of the notice.
This Court is of the view, that since it
being a private matrimonial dispute, an effort for 
mediation is required to be made in order to patch 
up the controversy/misunderstanding between the 
parties, and to reunite the family.
Issue administrative notice to the 
respondent no.2. The Registry is directed to 
ensure the service of the notice on the respondent 
no.2, and submit its report by the next date fixed.
Respondent no.2, would appear in person 
on the date to be so fixed by the Registry, so 
would be the applicants will also appear before 
this Court, in order to make an effort for  mediation.
As a consequence thereto, till the next date 
fixed or till the efforts for mediation are made by 
this Court, the proceedings of the Criminal Case 
No.5865 of 2022, “State Vs. Sameer Ahmed and 
others”, pending consideration before the court of 
4th Additional Chief Judicial Magistrate, 
Dehradun, would not be given effect to. 
(Sharad Kumar Sharma, J.)
 28.04.2023
NR/

COURT’S OR JUDGES’S ORDERS
09.06.2023 C482 No. 819 of 2023
Hon’ble Sharad Kumar Sharma, J.
Mr. Shorabh Sharma, Advocate, for 
the applicants.
Mr. Atul Kumar Shah, Deputy 
Advocate General, along with Mrs. Mamta 
Joshi, Brief Holder, for the State.
Mr. Syed Nadim, Advocate, for the 
respondent No. 2.
This Court, while issuing notices to 
the respondent No. 2, by an order dated 
28.04.2023, was initially of the opinion, that 
since the issue arises out of a matrimonial 
discord, there could be a possibility of 
settlement. The respondent No. 2 was 
noticed and she has put in appearance 
through Mr. Syed Nadim, Advocate.
This Court has interacted with her. 
She has expressly made a statement before 
this Court, that owing to the given set of 
circumstances, there is no possibility of 
settlement and there were various 
allegations which were levelled by her 
against the present applicants.
In that eventuality, there is no 
scope for referring the matter before the 
Mediator. The respondent who has now put 
in appearance, may file counter affidavit in 
furtherance of an order dated 28.04.2023, 
within a period of three weeks from today.
The interim order, already granted 
on 28.04.2023 would continue to operate  till the next date of listing.
Looking to the misbehaviour and 
the un-parliamentary vulgar dialect used by 
the respondent in her addresses, in the 
Court proceedings, this Court draws a suo 
moto contempt proceeding against the 
respondent. She is called upon to file a reply 
within a period of three weeks and would 
appear in person for the purposes of 
framing of a charge, if the reply is not found 
satisfactory.
(Sharad Kumar Sharma, J.)
 09.06.2023
Mahinder/

COURT’S OR JUDGES’S ORDERS
C482 No. 819 of 2023 
Hon’ble Sharad Kumar Sharma, J.
Mr. Kanti Ram Sharma, Advocate, for the 
applicants. 
Mr. V.K. Gemini, Deputy A.G., for the State of 
Uttarakhand. 
Mr. Syed Nadim, Advocate, for respondent 
No.2. 
Instead of filing a reply as sought for by the 
order dated 9th June, 2023, while drawing the suo 
moto contempt proceedings, the respondent No.2 has 
filed an application seeking to drop the contempt 
proceedings by extending an unconditional apology. 
Acceptance of apology would be only when 
there is plausible reply forthcoming from respondent 
No.2, and not as a matter of course, and particularly 
when the conduct of respondent No.2 maligns the 
prestige of the institution and the way litigant has to 
behave, when he or she is facing the proceedings 
before High Court. 
Reply to be submitted within three weeks. 
Put up this C482 Application before me 
immediately thereafter. 
Interim order dated 28.04.2023, to continue till 
the next date of listing. 
(Sharad Kumar Sharma, J.)
Dated 18.07.2023
Shiv
